WFRC and its partners maintain three planning models. They are developed in the open, and the pages below explain what each one does and where to find its documentation.

::: {.wfrc-blocks}
::: {.wfrc-block}
### Travel Demand Model

Forecasts how people travel on the region's roads and transit. Built with Mountainland Association of Governments (MAG).

Current release **{{< meta tdm-current >}}**

[Learn more](tdm.qmd){.btn .btn-sm}
:::

::: {.wfrc-block .mid}
### Real-Estate Market Model

Simulates where households and jobs may locate, from available land and market conditions, on the UrbanSim platform.

Current release **{{< meta remm-current >}}**

[Learn more](remm.qmd){.btn .btn-sm}
:::

::: {.wfrc-block .brick}
### Bike Demand Model

Estimates bicycle trips between small zones called microzones and assigns them to the bike network.

[Learn more](bdm.qmd){.btn .btn-sm}
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Want to use a model?
Access is by request. The [Get the model](get-the-model.qmd) guide explains who to ask, what to read first and where to download.
:::

## How the models fit together

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-alt: "Flow diagram. Land and policy inputs feed the Real-Estate Market Model, which produces household and job forecasts. These feed the Travel Demand Model, which returns travel accessibility to the Real-Estate Market Model. The Bike Demand Model is a separate model that uses microzones and the bike network."
flowchart LR
  A[Land, plans and<br/>control totals] --> B[Real-Estate<br/>Market Model]
  B --> H[Households<br/>and jobs] --> C[Travel Demand<br/>Model]
  C --> Q[Travel<br/>accessibility] --> B
  C --> D[Forecasts for plans<br/>and projects]
  E[Microzones and<br/>bike network] --> F[Bike Demand<br/>Model]
  F --> D
```

The Real-Estate Market Model's household and job projections drive trip generation in the Travel Demand Model. In turn, the Real-Estate Market Model uses travel accessibility from the Travel Demand Model when it predicts where development happens. The Bike Demand Model works at a finer scale, with its own zones and network.

## Coming next: an activity-based model

WFRC began an implementation project for an Activity-Based Model (ABM) in March 2026, expected to take about three years. It is not available yet. See the [WFRC models page](https://wfrc.utah.gov/resources/models-and-forecasting/){target="_blank"} for updates.

## Looking for something specific?

- The full documentation of record for every travel demand model version is on the [WFRC documentation site](https://wfrc.utah.gov/wftdm-docs/){target="_blank"}.
- Browse the apps built on these models in [Explore](../explore/index.qmd), or the supporting reports in [Reports & methods](../reports/index.qmd).
- To use a model, see [Get the model](get-the-model.qmd). To discuss a study, [contact the team](../contact/index.qmd).
